summary: Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and sinologist. She earned a BA from the University of Chicago (1968) and a master's (1970) and degree (1975) from Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia C. Stanley was a linguist and Indologist. She earned a BA from the University of Chicago (1966) and a PhD from the University of Texas at Austin (~1966–1972), later teaching at UT Austin, UT El Paso, Washington State, and University of Łódź (1976–1978).

Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who earned her PhD from the University of Kansas in 1983. She held curatorial and teaching posts before serving as professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2007–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a sinologist and Tibetologist. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under the doctoral supervision of Perry Link.

Patrick McAllister works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011) under Helmut Krasser, Karin Preisendanz, and Ernst Steinkellner, and has held researcher posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences since ~2012.

Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, Thomas Burrow, and R. C. Zaehner, and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University and UT Austin.

Patrick Pranke is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012), studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr.
Patrick Robert Cadell was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the East India Company College and at Balliol College, Oxford (~1889–1891).
Patrick Tugwell is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He is a doctoral graduate student at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

Patrul Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist philosopher and master in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu and Do Khyentse Yeshe Dorje, and taught disciples such as Minyak Kunzang Sonam and Shenphen Nangwa.
Paul Althaus was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1907–1910). He held an academic post at the University of Rostock (~1920–1925).

Paul Arnold Irzel was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Strasbourg and the University of Munich, and completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig (~1887–1890) under the supervision of Ernst Windisch.

Paul B. Courtright is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University, where he is attested from 1998 and is Professor Emeritus.

Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa as well as traditional teachers Geshe Yeshe Thapkay, Losang Yarphel, and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Carus was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He earned a PhD from Tübingen (~1874–1876) after studying at Greifswald and Strasbourg. He taught at Dresden Military Academy (~1876–1881) and founded and edited publications for Open Court Publishing Company.

Paul Copp is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at UMass Amherst and completed his PhD at Princeton under Stephen F. Teiser. He has held positions at Western Michigan University, Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, and the University of Chicago.

Paul Crowe is a sinology and religious studies scholar. He earned an MA from the University of Calgary (1990–1992) and a PhD from the University of British Columbia (1999–2005), and became an associate professor at Simon Fraser University in 2005.

Paul Dahlke was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 1900, he studied under Hikkaduwe Sri Sumangala Thera, Ñāṇissara Thera, and W. D. C. Wagiswara; he later founded Das Buddhistische Haus in 1924.

Paul David Devanandan was a religious studies scholar educated at Nizam College, Presidency University, Pacific School of Religion, and Yale (doctorate ~1927–1931). He taught at United Theological College (1932–1949) and directed the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society (1956).
